Hi, I'm a neuroscientist studying how the brain encodes, learns, and adapts. My current work is on the [Cell Types & Learning project](https://www.allenneuraldynamics.org/projects/cell-types-learning) at Allen Institute / Neural Dynamics, linking spatial transcriptomics to _in vivo_ neuronal activity during task learning.

Increasingly, that work involves developing algorithms for data acquisition, processing, and QC, deploying pipelines to scale, and building ML and agentic AI methods to make sense of large-scale, multimodal neuroscience data.

Recent focus areas:

- _In vivo_ two-photon imaging, spatial transcriptomics, multimodal data integration (neuronal activity, behavior, gene expression profile)
- Role of inhibitory interneurons in sensory perception and learning
- Building image data processing, QC, and analysis pipelines
- GCaMP8 transgenic mice validation and characterization
- Agentic AI-assisted pipeline development

Previously:

- Postdoctoral research @ University of Southern California (Hires Lab): Tactile shape perception and learning
- PhD research @ Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST; Dr. Yong Jeong's lab): Neurovascular coupling in Alzheimer's disease
- Master's research @ KAIST: Mitochonrial signaling in ROS-induced necrotic cell death
- Undergraduate research @ KAIST: Nonlinear interdependence in EEGs of PTSD patients
